name: Sika Interplant Systems Ltd
tagline: High-quality, accelerating small-cap aerospace/defence/space engineering + MRO house (~35% ROCE, FY26 revenue +41%, near debt-free) with a HEICO/Radiant repair-station tie-up and a HAL MoU - but ~61x trailing P/E, no concalls, and an unresolved moat debate
business_overview: Sika Interplant is an engineering-driven company serving Aerospace, Defence & Space (A&D) and automotive customers in India -- systems design and integration, component manufacture, interconnect / electrical module integration, MRO, and value-added distribution -- and is a licensed Indian Offset Partner for defence production. It is only BSE-listed, with promoter holding ~72% and a thin float. Since April 2025 it has been an authorised repair station in India for Radiant Power Corp (a HEICO company), starting with Dukane Seacom test-set calibration and intended to expand by part number in phases; it also has a HAL MoU for airborne SAR / MEDEVAC / aerial-firefighting / HADR cooperation.
fundamentals_table: ~35% ROCE / ~22-26% ROE -- sustained through 40%+ growth, asset-light
FY26 +40.8% to Rs 216.4 Cr (FY25 +37.3%); 5-yr CAGR ~18% and accelerating
FY26 PAT +43.8% to Rs 36.4 Cr; ~25% 5-yr CAGR; operating profit +47% (OPM ~22.5%)
AGM (Aug 2026): ~1.5x FY26 revenue, executable 6-24 months (excl. shorter MRO orders); FY25 intake ~Rs 264 Cr
Near debt-free; asset-light (fixed assets mostly land); low dividend payout (Rs 3.50/sh), reinvesting
fundamentals_narrative: High and consistent capital efficiency (~35% ROCE, ~25% 5-yr PAT CAGR) with a genuine multi-year acceleration: FY25 revenue +37%, FY26 +40.8% to Rs 216 Cr, FY26 operating profit +47% (OPM ~22.5%) and PAT +43.8% to Rs 36.4 Cr, on a near-debt-free, asset-light base. The order book has run ahead of revenue for years (AGM guidance ~1.5x FY26 revenue). The deep read leaves the quality intact and adds no red flags, but sharpens two caveats: (1) valuation is rich and now confirmed -- ~61x trailing P/E and ~10x sales, which already prices many years of 35%+ compounding plus a HEICO/HAL channel conversion; (2) disclosure is genuinely thin -- management holds no earnings calls, filings have carried occasional errors, and forward order flow cannot be tracked between results. Quarterly numbers are lumpy (Q4 FY26 PAT -17.5% QoQ) because revenue is project- and milestone-driven.
technical_read: Not independently pulled beyond noting the stock hit record highs in mid-2025 on strong March-2025-quarter results and the Radiant/HEICO news; price ~Rs 1,011 as of late Aug 2026.
sentiment_summary: Sporadic thread, 50 of ~75 posts read spanning 2019-2026. Long-running debate on whether Sika has a moat: a 25-year aviation-industry veteran argued Indian AMO/MRO economics are structurally poor (thin margins, no local overhaul-shop infrastructure) and that private players get stuck making non-critical parts. Against that, execution has been consistently strong -- multiple 'blockbuster' quarters, ~2x-revenue order wins, the April-2025 appointment as an authorised repair station for Radiant Power Corp (a HEICO group company; HEICO is a ~USD 32 bn NYSE-listed aerospace major) opening a potential large-order channel, and a HAL MoU for airborne SAR / medevac / firefighting.
community_signal: Gautam_Chopra (trusted, elevated) tracked Sika positively through 2023 ('30% topline growth, 75% PAT jump QoQ', 'Rs 117 Cr new orders'). Mohit_baid (elevated) posted a chart in early 2026 without commentary. No strong, dated buy-conviction call in the recent window.

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium. FY26 confirmed the quality (growth accelerated to +41%, ~35% ROCE, near debt-free) and there are no new red flags, but four_box scores 2.5 with valuation a clear 'no' (~61x trailing P/E) and moat only 'weak' (narrow HEICO scope, Tier-2/3 client skew, thin disclosure). The '10x-in-2-3-years' label is retained via the un-ignorable-growth carve-out, which caps conviction at Medium with an unconfirmed caveat.

value_chain.note: Strong structural defence/MRO tailwind (offset obligations, MRO GST cut 18%->5%, fleet growth) but capital is flooding into Indian A&D small-caps and multiples are rich across the space (valuation glut more than a physical-capacity glut). Sika's edge is OEM approvals + a HEICO repair-station tie-up; the open question (25-yr industry veteran on the VP thread) is whether Indian private MRO economics stay thin and players get stuck on non-critical work.

verdict_headline: High-quality, accelerating small-cap A&D engineering + MRO compounder (~35% ROCE, FY26 +41%) with a real HEICO/HAL catalyst -- '10x' bucket retained on un-ignorable growth, but conviction cut to MEDIUM (capped) by a ~61x multiple, thin disclosure and an unresolved moat
verdict_reasoning: FY26 confirmed and improved the thesis: revenue +40.8% (accelerating from +37% FY25), PAT +43.8%, operating profit +47%, ~35% ROCE sustained, near debt-free -- genuine multi-year quality at a Rs 216 Cr base with structural defence/MRO tailwinds

four_box score 2.5: tailwind and tam 'yes' (small-cap, structural tailwind), moat 'weak' (sustained ROCE and OEM approvals are real, but the HEICO scope is narrow and the Indian-MRO-economics debate is unresolved), valuation 'no' (~61x trailing P/E / ~10x sales already prices the compounding plus a HEICO/HAL conversion)

Per the score-2.0-2.5 rule the default would be 'neither'; the un-ignorable-growth carve-out (FY25 +37%, FY26 +41%, ~35% ROCE, pristine balance sheet, order book ~1.5x revenue) is invoked to retain '10x-in-2-3-years' -- which caps conviction at MEDIUM with an explicit 'unconfirmed' caveat. Realistic base case is a 2-4x; the true 10x needs a large HEICO-channel order to convert

Cut from Medium-High to Medium on the valuation box and disclosure, not on any deterioration. No red-flag tier. Revisit: HEICO/Radiant scope broadening, any HAL MoU conversion, order-intake announcements, and RPT/working-capital detail (unverified this pass)

four_box.note: valuation is the clear 'no' (~61x trailing P/E, ~10x sales -- many years of 35%+ compounding plus a HEICO/HAL conversion already in the price); moat 'weak' (sustained ~35% ROCE and OEM approvals are real evidence of an edge, but the HEICO scope is narrow, clients skew Tier-2/3, and Indian MRO economics are debated). tailwind + tam (structural defence/MRO, tiny Rs 216 Cr base) carry it to 2.5; the '10x' label is retained via the un-ignorable-growth carve-out (FY25 +37%, FY26 +41%, ~35% ROCE, near debt-free) with conviction capped at Medium and an 'unconfirmed' caveat.
